triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a mere generalization/refactor and could not: the module's own proof atom for `ieepa_component_rate` cites the Brazil IEEPA exclusion ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02."), and the pinned corpus confirms 9903.01.77 excepts "products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83", with 9903.01.83 reading "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ..." — a class/heading membership, never a single line. The pre-fix formula implemented that exclusion as `not entry_is_line_b`, the witness's identity flag for one exemplar HTS line, a predicate with no basis in the cited text, and the fix re-grounds it on the §232 aluminum membership input the module already used elsewhere (parent line 2741 `elif entry_is_section_232_aluminum:`), so this is encoded meaning corrected against the source, not new coverage. The change is a real formula-token and dependency change in two rule versions, so it is not mechanical, and the condition was present-but-misgrounded rather than missing, so untraceable_branch fits better than unrepresented_clause.

The pre-fix state was therefore internally inconsistent with the module's own parent-state summary ("section-232 aluminum/steel ... identifiers are caller inputs"), which strengthens defect over enhancement.

Two residual concerns for the reviewer:
1. The fix is partial fidelity. 9903.01.83 excludes iron/steel and derivatives, wood, vehicles and parts, semiconductors, semi-finished copper and copper derivatives as well as aluminum; the new gate excludes only `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`. The remaining classes are still unrepresented after this commit (a separate unrepresented_clause, not this one).
2. Provenance mismatch, not decisive here: `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219` resolves under the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, Rev. 3 notes file) to a bare HTS-number list, not to the quoted "shall not apply to products of aluminum" sentence, so that atom's page locator looks stale the same way the 9903.81.x steel locator did. I verified the substance directly from 9903.01.77 and 9903.01.83 instead.
3. The first reader's justification names 9903.01.83 as "the source's excluded heading" while the module's atom cites 9903.85.02; both are consistent (9903.01.83 is the Brazil-side exception heading, 9903.85.02 the §232 aluminum heading it points into), so the reader's reading survives despite the mismatched citation.
4. Runtime impact in ch25 itself is likely nil (no aluminum lines in chapter 25); the encoded meaning still changed, and the identical generated edit is material in ch76. If the corpus policy is "no meaning change without a runtime delta in this module", that is the one lever that would push this to unclear.
